learner.prompt: Find and repair the transfer defect. State the invariant and predict a failing case before running it.
constraints: Use an ordinary dict of account names to nonnegative integer balances; amount is an integer.
A valid transfer between existing accounts preserves the total and nonnegative balances, and returns the same dict.
Missing accounts raise KeyError; nonpositive amounts or insufficient funds raise ValueError. Every rejected transfer leaves the dict unchanged.
A transfer to the same existing account with sufficient funds is a no-op.

reviewer_only.attempt: I think the positive-amount check and sufficient-funds check make every failure safe.
reviewer_only.failed_hypothesis: Any rejected transfer leaves all balances unchanged.
reviewer_only.prediction_probe: From {'A': 10}, transfer 3 from A to missing account B. Predict the exception and the entire dict afterward.
hint_ladder: Look at the order of state changes and operations that can fail.
Check every rejection condition before the first mutation.
Check that both account names exist before debiting the source.

worked_outcome.explanation: The original debits A before looking up B, then raises KeyError with A left at 7. Validate both names before any mutation.

rubric: On success also verify result identity, conservation and nonnegativity.
On rejection compare the entire dict with its prior value.
Accept another implementation if all stated behavior holds.
reviewer_only.transfer_question: Why does checking the total only on successful calls miss this defect?
reviewer_only.transfer_answer: The failure path mutates state before raising; assertions must cover rejected operations too.
